description: Library can write a small, correct, idiomatic Rust utility with passing unit tests from a one-line ask.
task: Write a small Rust utility `fn slugify(input: &str) -> String` that converts arbitrary text into a URL-safe slug: lowercase the input, replace any run of non-alphanumeric ASCII characters with a single hyphen, and trim leading/trailing hyphens. Place it in a crate that builds with `cargo test`, and include unit tests covering the empty string, leading/trailing punctuation, mixed case, and collapsing runs of separators. The code must compile and all tests must pass.

library.note: Library-ON. The Rust specialist agent, with the full skills + subagents library available.

baseline.prompt: Write the Rust crate directly from your own knowledge. Do NOT read, load, or invoke any library skills. Do NOT dispatch subagents or use any /-commands or workflows. Produce the crate files yourself in this turn.
baseline.note: Library-OFF baseline. Instruction-suppressed: a vanilla agent told to use none of the library's machinery.

deterministic_check.spec: Stage the produced crate into <dir> and run `run-checker.sh cargo-test <dir>`, which invokes `cargo test` in the crate root. PASS iff the build succeeds and every test passes (exit code 0). This is the Tier-0 spine — it GATES.

rubric.note: Tier-2 judge layer — INFORMS only, never gates. Pairwise per-dimension winner+margin; default-reject posture (judge conservatively when evidence for a dimension is weak).

dimensions.asks: Does slugify implement all three rules (lowercase, collapse non-alphanumeric runs to one hyphen, trim edge hyphens) without off-by-one or Unicode-vs-ASCII bugs the prompt's edge cases would expose?
Do the unit tests actually exercise the named edge cases (empty, leading/trailing punctuation, mixed case, separator runs) with assertions on exact output, vs a single happy-path smoke test?
Idiomatic iterator/char-class handling and ownership (no needless allocations, no unwrap-on-everything), &str in / String out as specified, vs a transliterated-from-another-language style.
Solves exactly the asked problem in one focused function; no gratuitous dependencies, config, trait abstractions, or i18n scope creep.
